newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index gains, activity decreases.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index gains, activity decreases.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share gained marginally on Tuesday amid reduced activity in quiet trading, brokers and bourse officials said.
The index gained 2.68 points to stand at 3061.57. Turnover was posted at 6.654 million shillings traded on 184,634 shares from 7.205 million shares traded on 194,345 shares on Monday.
"The market traded like a retail outlet, with no major movements or lots being sold," a broker said.
The Nairobi bourse has been depressed for the last month boosted occasionally by big lots traded on the special boards.
"Most brokers have a wait and see attitude, beginning the trading session quite actively, quiet in the middle, and then rushing at the end," a bourse official said.

Key shares in the financials were on average unchanged. Barclays Bank traded 6,314 shares at unchanged 96, Kenya Commercial Bank traded 12,140 shares at an unchanged 56, Housing Finance Company traded 8,650 shares at 20.50 from 20.75 while foreigners bought 6,000 shares of Jubilee Insurance at 36 from 39.
"There's been reduced interest in the financials this week which is why they are slipping slightly," a senior broker said.

There has been speculation in the market that the collapse of Kenya Finance Bank would have a negative impact in the financial sector. The bank was declared insolvent by the Central Bank of Kenya on Nov 1, 1996.

"The drop in interest has nothing really to do with the liquidation of Kenya Finance Bank. In fact, we expect the bigger banks to benefit because they are perceived as being more stable. The most likely losers are the small banks," he added.
Brokers say that the case is isolated.

"We cannot really say that this will affect the market the way an epidemic would, and even more so because the listing requirements for the market tend to attract the more stable institutions," a broker said.
Uchumi continued to attract investor interest with 37,523 shares being traded at an unchanged 50.
"At 47, there has been very little supply for the share, even if demand has been there. People are more willing to buy at 50," another broker said.
Foreigners bought 1,079 shares of Kakuzi at 96 from 96.50.
